hypotheses.statement: The 1 mOhm gate-independent Sswfail branch switching on near the fault creates a hard topology/conductance transition that the ideal zero-volt diode sense branch cannot converge through.
hypotheses.evidence: Sswfail is in parallel with Msw; Vdboost2sense is an ideal 0 V branch probe.

hypotheses.statement: The failed-short edge coincides with mixed-signal protection/PWM transitions and ideal zero-volt source probes, producing a locally stiff algebraic event independent of the physical branch current.
hypotheses.evidence: The deck uses 1 ns PWL fault/control edges, ideal probes, and mixed-signal bridge elements.

minimal_discriminating_fixture: Construct a standalone micro-deck from the retained switch, diode, Vdboost2sense, and Vchannel topology with the same SWFAIL model and solver options, but a normalized event at t=0 over a tens-of-nanoseconds window. Run two static variants in a future experiment: remove Sswfail (H1 control) and retain Sswfail while suppressing the controller/PWL edge (H2 control). Compare convergence and timestep collapse at the Vdboost2sense branch; this distinguishes the candidates without replaying the 0.65 s campaign, but cannot establish full-deck behavior.
evidence_boundary: Only regular stop.txt, host.stderr, host.stdout, case.cir, and prior review documents were read. No FIFO, raw trace, solver, process control, or source mutation was performed.
